scoring_justification: The checker recomputes the dispersion and absorption spectra from the published equations and material parameters, then scores peak positions and intensities against the agent's output.

hidden_assets.purpose: Recomputed reference absorption spectra and dispersion classification using the physical model and material parameters as given in the task.
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Derived from the paper's equations (1) and (2) together with publicly known dielectric function parameters (Al Drude, ZnTe Lorentz oscillator).
hidden_assets.generation_method: The checker reconstructs the exact absorption and dispersion functions internally using numpy/scipy with the same parameter values as provided to the agent.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: The reference is a deterministic solution of the same physical model; it is consistent with the paper's results and avoids fabrication.

schema.description: wavenumber (cm-1) float, in_plane_wavevector_q (cm-1) float, branch_type string ('radiative' or 'nonradiative')

outputs.description: Dispersion branches of TM polaritons for a vacuum-ideal dielectric (ε2=5.8, d=10 μm) - Al mirror structure. The checker verifies presence of at least one radiative and one nonradiative branch and correct classification.
p‑polarized absorption spectrum of the ideal dielectric film on Al mirror at φ=20°.
p‑polarized absorption spectrum of a pure ZnTe film on Al mirror at φ=20°.
p‑polarized absorption spectrum of a Cd₀.₀₅Zn₀.₉₅Te film on Al mirror at φ=20°, showing resonance‑enhanced absorption near 170 cm⁻¹.

output_contract.notes: All absorption spectra are computed for the same geometry: prism and gap ε=1, incidence angle φ=20°. The CdZnTe film includes an additional impurity oscillator near 170 cm⁻¹. The checker will detect absorption peaks and compare their positions and relative intensities to hidden reference values derived from the paper’s figures. For the dispersion data, the checker will audit branch classification.

steps.description: Verify that at least one radiative and one nonradiative branch are present and that branch_type correctly follows q <= 2πν for radiative.
Check that the spectrum contains a peak near the expected interference mode frequency (as computed from pure ZnTe) and that its absorption is significantly enhanced relative to the pure ZnTe case.
